CandidateAttempt.description:
One candidate identity oneharness attempted for a single invocation — the
harness (and variant/model) it tried, and what came of it.

Under `run_mode = "fallback"` oneharness attempts candidates in priority order
and stops at the first that runs the task, so an invocation can have several of
these: the ones it fell through, then the one that ran. This is the typed form
of oneharness's per-candidate record — the thing that lets a consumer attribute
a failure to a *side* (agent vs judge) and an *identity* (which harness, which
account) instead of grepping a message.

available.description: Whether oneharness found the harness binary.

error.description: oneharness's human-readable problem statement for a failed attempt.

exit_code.description: The harness process's exit code, when it ran to completion.

failure_kind.description:
oneharness's normalized failure reason (`auth`, `rate_limit`,
`model_not_found`, `quota`, `tool_deferred`), when it classified one.

harness_id.description:
Base id, or `<base>:<variant>` when a named preset selected the identity —
the selector that reproduces this candidate.

history_id.description:
The oneharness history record written for this attempt, when history was
on — the handle `oneharness history show` resolves.

model.description: The model this candidate ran with, when one was requested.

ran.description: Whether this is the candidate that actually ran the turn.

session_id.description: The harness's own continuation id, when it exposed one.

variant.description: The named preset, when this candidate came from a composed harness id.

FailureDetail.description: The failure itself, with the classification a caller branches on.

kind.description:
The provider failure category, when the failure came from a provider and
was classified (`auth`, `quota`, `timeout`, `spawn`, `protocol`, …).

message.description: The human-readable failure, exactly as it is printed on stderr.

FellThrough.description:
One candidate a fallback chain fell through, with oneharness's reason token
(`not-installed`, `spawn-error`, `auth`, `quota`, `model-not-found`,
`rate-limit`).

reason.description: Why it could not run the task at all.

HarnessAttribution.description:
What oneharness attempted for one provider invocation, placed on the side and
turn that made the call.

candidates.description: Every attempted candidate, in the order oneharness tried them.

fell_through.description: Candidates a fallback chain routed around, in priority order.

history_file.description: The oneharness history session file this invocation appended to.

ran.description: The candidate that ran the turn, by composed id; `null` when none could.

role.description: Which side of the conversation made this call.

turn_index.description: One-based invocation index within the role.

PartyTelemetry.description: Aggregated measurements for one side of a run.

model_ms.description: Model/provider elapsed time, when every contributing invocation reported it.

session_ids.description: Native oneharness session IDs in first-seen order, without duplicates.

time_to_first_token_ms.description: Time to first token from the first invocation that reported it.

tool_ms.description: Tool elapsed time, when every contributing invocation reported it.

usage.description: Strictly aggregated usage; each field is present only when every invocation knew it.

ProviderErrorKind.description:
Machine-readable classification of a provider failure.

The category a consumer branches on instead of matching substrings in the
human message (the reason this exists: a timeout is
[`ProviderErrorKind::Timeout`], not `message.contains("timed out")`). It maps
directly onto `oneharness`'s normalized `failure_kind`. The set is closed on
purpose; a label this version does not recognize becomes
[`ProviderErrorKind::Other`] rather than a new, unhandled string.

oneOf.description: Authentication/authorization failed (missing or rejected credentials).
The provider rate-limited the call; a backoff-and-retry may succeed.
The harness/vendor does not recognize the requested model.
The account's quota or billing limit is exhausted.
A transient server-side overload.
The call exceeded its deadline.

The run was torn down before it finished because it was **cancelled** —
the caller stopped the turn, or the host was signalled. Distinct from
[`ProviderErrorKind::Timeout`], which was given its full deadline and
exceeded it: a cancelled call says nothing about whether the harness was
healthy, so it is not a reason to give up on the environment.
The provider process could not be started (binary missing, not runnable).

The provider ran but produced output that violated the protocol
(unparseable envelope, missing results, malformed verdict).
A classified failure that does not map to a more specific category.

SessionLink.description: Authoritative linkage from a onejudge role/turn to a native oneharness run.

finished_at.description: Upstream UTC invocation-finish timestamp, or `null` when not observed.

history_id.description: Native oneharness history record identity, when history was available.

role.description: Which side of the conversation owns the invocation.

turn_index.description: One-based invocation index within the role.

Telemetry.description: Timing, usage, and native linkage for the complete agent+judge run.

attribution.description:
Which harness identities each invocation attempted, in invocation order.
Empty when the provider reports no candidate identities.

orchestration_ms.description: Non-negative wall-time remainder after measured model and tool work.

sessions.description: Native session linkage records in invocation order.

wall_ms.description: Monotonic duration from task-loop entry through final result assembly.

TelemetryRole.description: The side of the evaluated conversation that owns an invocation.

oneOf.description: The skill/agent under evaluation.
The simulated user, supervisor, or final evaluator.

Usage.description:
Token / cost usage for one provider call, or a running total.

Each field is independently optional because not every harness reports every
signal (cost is commonly absent on subscription auth, and cache counts only
when the harness surfaces prompt-cache reads/writes). `None` means "no
signal", never "zero" — so a total stays `None` until something reports a real
number, then accumulates.

cache_read_tokens.description:
Prompt tokens served from the provider's prompt cache — a cheap read of a
previously-written prefix — when the harness reports them. `None` when the
harness does not surface cache counts, never `0` as a guess.

cache_write_tokens.description:
Prompt tokens written to the provider's prompt cache (a.k.a. cache
creation), when the harness reports them. `None` when not surfaced.

cost_usd.description: Total cost in USD, when reported.

failure_report.description:
The machine-readable document a `--format json` run writes when it produced no
[`Report`]: why it failed, and the telemetry — including per-invocation harness
attribution — recorded before it did.

Stamped with the same [`SCHEMA_VERSION`](crate::SCHEMA_VERSION) as a report, so
one number describes both halves of the CLI's JSON surface. Additive: before
this existed a failed `--format json` run wrote nothing at all.

error.description: Why the run did not complete.

schema_version.description: The contract version this document was serialized under.

telemetry.description:
Timing, usage, and per-invocation harness attribution recorded before the
failure; absent when nothing ran.

failure_report.title: FailureReport

events.description:

ToolEvent.description:
One normalized tool-call / action event the skill took during a turn, lifted
from `oneharness`'s `events` array (its `--events` output). Harness-agnostic,
so a consumer can inspect shell commands, file edits, and tool uses across any
harness, not just the final text. `input` is the structured, tool-shaped args
so a consumer can match on the command string or file path without re-parsing.

`input` is free-form JSON, so `Message`/`Transcript` are `PartialEq` but not
`Eq`.

index.description: Position within the run, so ordering ("did X before Y") is expressible.

input.description: Structured tool arguments (the command, the file path); `None` when none.

kind.description: `tool_call` (the skill invoked a tool) or `tool_result` (the observation).

name.description:
Normalized tool name where knowable (e.g. `bash`, `edit_file`); `None` for
a `tool_result` or when the harness did not name it.

output.description: The result/observation text, when the transcript exposed it.

messages.description: The turns in order, oldest first.

report.description:
A judged run: the transcript, the verdicts scored against it, aggregated
usage, and whether a streaming sink short-circuited the run — stamped with the
[`SCHEMA_VERSION`] of the contract that produced it.

Build one from an [`Outcome`](crate::Outcome) with
[`Outcome::into_report`](crate::Outcome::into_report), or directly with
[`Report::new`].

assessment.description: A free-text judgement requested by the caller, if any.

completion_reason.description: Why the per-turn supervisor declared the task complete, if it did.

schema_version.description: The contract version this report was serialized under.

stopped_early.description: Whether a streaming sink asked to short-circuit the run.

telemetry.description: Timing, per-party usage, and native oneharness session linkage.

transcript.description: The full conversation transcript, with tool events on assistant turns.

usage.description: Aggregated usage across every provider call (`None` if nothing reported).

verdicts.description: The verdicts scored against the transcript, in the order they were added.

report.title: Report

EvalConfig.description: One eval scored against the finished transcript.

kind.description: Boolean (a pass/fail verdict) or numeric (a score on a scale).

scale.description:
The inclusive `[min, max]` scale for a numeric eval; ignored (and rejected)
for a boolean one. Defaults to `[0, 10]`.

oneOf.description: A yes/no verdict.
A score on a `[min, max]` scale.

ProviderConfig.description:
Which backend runs the harness. A flat, strict struct (rather than an
internally-tagged enum, which serde cannot pair with `deny_unknown_fields`):
[`ProviderConfig::resolve`] checks that only the chosen `kind`'s fields are set
and turns it into a validated [`ProviderSpec`], so a misplaced-but-spelled-right
key (e.g. `bin` under `kind: command`) is still a loud error.

judge.description: `split`: the backend that judges and plays the simulated user.

judge_config.description:
`oneharness`: the oneharness config file the judge / simulated user run
under, passed as `oneharness run --config <path>` (default
`oneharness.judge.toml`). This is where the judge-side harness/model
selection lives.

skill.description: `split`: the backend that runs the agent's turns.

stream.description:
`oneharness`: the agent-side binary speaks the **streamed provider
protocol** (`docs/streaming.md`) — NDJSON tool events as they occur, then a
terminal report line. Default `false` (one buffered report document).

ProviderKind.description:
The provider backends the CLI can build. One enum is the single source for
both the YAML `kind:` (via `Deserialize`) and the `--provider` flag (via
clap's `ValueEnum`), so the two surfaces cannot drift.

oneOf.description: Shell out to the `oneharness` CLI (the default).
A custom command speaking the JSON-lines protocol.
Compose a skill-runner with a separate judge / simulated-user backend.

UserConfig.description: The simulated user that supervises the agent and drives the loop.

done_when.description:
A plain-English completion condition; when the judge decides it holds, the
loop ends. Without it the loop ends at `max_turns` or when the agent
declares itself done.

max_turns.description: The assistant-turn cap for this run.

persona.description: How the simulated user behaves (their instructions).

run_config.description:
The whole YAML config for one run. Field defaults let a minimal file (just a
`task`) work, while `deny_unknown_fields` makes a typo'd key a hard error
instead of a silently-ignored setting.

assessment.description: Optional prompt for a free-text judgement of the finished transcript.

evals.description: Optional criteria to score the finished transcript with.

provider.description:
Which backend runs the harness (and judges / plays the user).

Harness/model **selection** is no longer a onejudge concern: the agent side
uses oneharness's discovered `oneharness.toml`, and the judge side uses the
`provider.judge_config` file (default `oneharness.judge.toml`). Scaffold both
with `onejudge init`.

session.description:
The caller-owned session name threaded across turns; defaults to
`onejudge`.

skill.description:
Path to a **skill** directory (containing a `SKILL.md`) whose instruction
body seeds the system prompt. Resolved relative to the config file's
directory (or the working dir for a flag-only run). Optional — combine it
with `system_prompt`, use either alone, or neither.

system_prompt.description:
Extra system-prompt text for the harness. When a `skill` is also set, this
comes **first** and the skill's body is appended after it.

task.description:
The task to drive to completion. May instead be supplied by `--task`
(`-` reads stdin); required by the time the plan is built.

user.description:
The simulated user / supervisor that drives the loop. Omit for a
single-turn run (the agent answers once).

stream_event.description:
One streamed tool event delivered live to an [`Engine::run_streaming`] sink,
tagged with the turn it belongs to.

It is also the payload of an `event` line in the **streamed protocol**
(`docs/streaming.md`) that `onejudge run --stream` publishes — the line adds
the `"type": "event"` discriminator around exactly these fields, so an SDK
hands this type straight to its own event callback.
